verdict.rationale: Lithic documents virtual card creation via API, card-level Authorization Rules on attributes like MCC, card spend limits, and ASA for custom per-transaction approval. Together these let a developer build tightly scoped cards. However, the evidence never mentions a native single-use or merchant-locked card type, so one-purchase, one-merchant, exact-amount behavior would have to be assembled from rules, limits, or custom ASA logic. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented single-use card type, merchant-locking to a specific merchant, exact-amount enforcement, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
